newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: L&G Australian unit targets index funds.
newsitem.headline: L&G Australian unit targets index funds.

text.p: Legal & General Group Plc's (L&G) Australian unit said on Monday it would aim to win up to half of all mandates for index funds in Australia in the next 12 months.

L&G Australia said it has about A$1.2 billion under management in index funds, run out of Britain, but is bringing the business to Australia as part of expansion plans in what it believes will be a fast growing area of investment management.

Tim Batho, who will head up the index fund arm, told reporters index funds now accounted for about 7-8 percent of the A$350 billion Australian market, compared with 20 percent in the UK and more than 30 percent in the U.S.
"There is no doubt (Australia) will follow overseas trends and its is conceivable that the percentage under index fund management could be at least twice as high as it is now," Batho said.
Index funds attempt to mirror the performance of a chosen index, compared with active management where funds attempt to outperform the market.
L&G would focus primarily on the wholesale end of the market where there were currently several mandates in the billions of dollars, said investment services head Tim Hyde.
"I'd like to believe we are going to get between one-third and one-half of the mandates that are going to come up in the next twelve months," Batho said.
He agreed that Australia's benchmark index, the All Ordinaries, was more concentrated than indices in Britain or the U.S., but said big issues coming to the market would help diversification.
These included the partial sale of telecommunications company Telstra Corp and the proposed demutualisation of insurance and fund management group, Australian Mutual Provident Society (AMP).
The L&G group manages about A$105 billion of funds worldwide, half of which are in index related funds.
